title: The Love Letters Project
bodyHtml:
The Love Letters Project

On a mission to bring back the Lost Art of Love Letters. With the simple premise of putting more Love into our world, the Love Letters project was launched in January of 2016.

Lost Art of Love Letters gives the public a moment to slow down and reflect on whom or what touches their heart. The participant is engaged by a variety of art mediums as well as visual & thought engaging prompts and are brought through a process using art, poetry and writing to create a Love Letter. Many types of Love Letters are created. Some are used for political action & environmental appreciation, such as Love Letters to the Sea. Others are used for mental wellness, personal introspection and growth such as Love Letters to Self. Working with diverse audiences in various settings, collaborations have been formed with environmental organizations, mental health organizations, environmental protection agencies, education facilities, museums, rehabs, shelters and galleries in California and abroad.

Lost Art of Love Letters not only transforms the participant but the viewers and receivers of these creations of Art. Showing people the power of using their Art & words to care for what we Love.

title: Ecoversities
bodyHtml:
Ecoversities

About Ecoversities

Ecoversities is an evolving network of people, communities, and learning spaces working to reimagine education in service of life, local territories, and the Earth. Our specific group, or node, is part of Ecoversities Abya Yala, which connects initiatives across Latin America that understand learning as something created through practice, relationships, conversation, and in-person encounters among different territories, languages, and ways of knowing. Together, we are exploring more autonomous and community-rooted ways of embodying learning.

Through August 17th, fundraising efforts are being done in partnership with CoFundEco. The funds raised will support the creation and testing of the first series of digital learning experiences based on knowledge developed in Latin American territories. Funds will help cover the time, tools, translation, subtitles, editing, and basic platform expenses needed to produce accessible prototypes. We will share this through an existing digital platform, and document the process so other nodes can adapt it. This is part of a broader creative effort to build our own funding ecosystem: a sustainable circuit in which learning materials circulate, connect initiatives, generate resources, and help sustain future projects, rather than continuing to depend only on donations as we move forward. Your support will allow these educational and community-building efforts to become self-sustaining.

Support Ecoversities Today!

Your support is greatly appreciated!

title: Ancient Cacao
bodyHtml:
Become a Friend of Montegrande

Help Reveal the Ancient Story of Cacao and the 6,000+ Year Legacy of Huaca Montegrande. Your charitable gift supports ASICAMPE (the Association for the Scientific Investigation of the Peruvian Amazon), the nonprofit organization leading the study and preservation of Huaca Montegrande in Jaén, Peru – a 6,000+ year-old sanctuary and ceremonial temple that is reshaping our understanding of the earliest civilizations of the Americas and the ancient story of cacao. Hidden beneath the city of Jaen for millennia, this extraordinary site is now entering a pivotal phase of discovery. With no government funding, ASICAMPE depends entirely on philanthropic support. Our immediate goal is to raise $20,000–$50,000 to continue this critical phase of excavation, scientific research, conservation, and cultural stewardship. By becoming a Friend of Montegrande, you are helping reveal and preserve one of the world’s most important archaeological and biocultural treasures while advancing our long-term vision of securing international recognition, including UNESCO World Heritage status, so that this extraordinary legacy will be protected, celebrated, and shared with future generations. Thank you for helping write the next chapter in the story of Huaca Montegrande.

title: Powering Clean Cooking with Comics
bodyHtml:
Powering Clean Cooking with Comics: A Biogas Education Pilot

What if everyday food waste could become clean cooking fuel, natural fertilizer, and a visual story that transforms communities?

Across Haiti and Africa, biogas practitioners are already helping families and communities turn organic waste into clean cooking fuel, natural fertilizer, and new opportunities.To help these local solutions reach even more people, practitioners need visual, story-driven tools that make biogas easier to understand, trust, and share.

We are that. By merging Kathy Puffer’s biogas education work with the vibrant art of Haitian illustrator Thony Loui (Spider Whale Studios LLC), this pilot brings clean energy to life through mobile-first visual storytelling.

The Opportunity:

As biogas adoption continues to grow, practitioners are looking for outreach tools that are as innovative and accessible as the solutions they champion. Educational materials that work well in community settings, on mobile devices, and across different literacy levels can help more people understand how biogas fits into their daily lives.

What We Learned in the Field:

This project began by listening. A survey of 15 biogas entrepreneurs and practitioners in Haiti and across Africa revealed a clear priority: practical, visual tools that support community education and engagement.

Practitioners shared that effective outreach materials should be:

• Easy to understand
• Mobile-friendly
• Visually engaging
• Designed for sharing in the community with WhatsApp

They emphasized the value of story-based learning that helps people quickly grasp key concepts, remember them, and share them with others.

This pilot project uses mobile-first comics, character-based education, and short animation to make clean energy relatable, accessible, and easy to share. Through the eyes of Maya Limyè (our community guide) and Tanama (her curious companion), we turn complex science into stories that households, smallholder farmers, and schools can understand in minutes instead of hours.

How We Are Making an Impact:

  • Character-Driven Education:
    We turn complex science into stories that families can understand in minutes.
  • Built for Mobile:
    We are creating WhatsApp-friendly comics, graphics, and short animations designed specifically for the devices communities already use every day.
  • Empowering Local Practitioners:
    Providing households, smallholder farmers, and schools with a practical toolkit to easily share the benefits of sustainable waste management.

Your Impact:

Your support funds a practical outreach toolkit including pilot comic strips, visual system guides, and a comprehensive plan for translation. Together, we can make clean energy visual, memorable, and trusted.

Your Support Will Help Create:

  • Pilot educational comic strip
  • Biogas infographic series
  • Biodigester system illustration
  • WhatsApp-ready graphics
  • Social media outreach materials
  • Printable coloring book
  • Educational poster
  • Translation planning (English, Haitian Creole, and French)
  • Short AI-assisted educational animation

title: Ho’okele Industries – A free market solution to over fishing
bodyHtml:
Ho’olekele Industries

A Free Market Solution to Over Fishing


The Ocean Crisis and the Power of Permaculture After decades at sea, I have watched vibrant marine ecosystems turn into oceanic deserts. I have come to realize that sustainable aquaculture is the only real way to save our oceans from overfishing. Ho’okele Industries is dedicated to making this a reality, but our approach goes far beyond simply changing the seafood supply chain. We are building a visionary loop rooted in permaculture, education, and eating locally. When we change the way we eat and interact with our local environment, we take the pressure off our global seas.

From Backyard Hobby to Community Resilience At our core, we are an educational movement. We are teaching people about the fun and fulfillment of raising fish right in their own backyards. What starts as a rewarding hobby can scale into a community lifeline. At Ho’okele, we have proven that with a small-scale, sustainable setup, you can feed your family, feed your friends, feed your neighborhood, and still have a little left over to sell. We are actively creating a new generation of sustainable micro-farmers who understand that producing and eating locally is the key to global conservation.

“The Fishmonger” & The Free-Market Approach To empower these new sustainable farmers and connect them directly to consumers, we invented “The Fishmonger.” This proprietary, 300-gallon, solar-powered stock tank is a completely off-grid retail unit. It allows local farmers to sell live, fresh, sustainably raised seafood directly to their communities. We believe the free-market approach is the best way to drive real environmental change. By placing Fishmongers in community farm stands and local grocers, we provide an irresistible, hyper-local alternative to commercially over-fished seafood.

Put Wind in Our Sails Our ultimate goal is a self-sustaining, free-market ecosystem powered by educated, local farmers. But to launch this fleet and expand our educational outreach, we need you. Your tax-deductible contribution through the Abundant Earth Foundation will put the crucial wind in our sails. 100% of all funds earmarked for the “Fishmonger Project” will go directly toward manufacturing new solar-powered units and empowering communities to grow their own sustainable seafood. Partner with us today, and help us prove that saving the oceans begins in our own backyards.

Best regards,

Captain Jonas Molloy Founder, Ho’okele Industries

title: ReGenerOsa Collective
bodyHtml:
ReGenerOsa Collective

Strengthening the people, projects, and processes that steward 2.5% of the Earth’s biodiversity.

The ReGenerOsa Collective raises funds and other forms of support for its bioregional fund to then redistribute to local people, projects, and processes that are working to protect and restore one of the most biodiverse places in the world, the Osa Peninsula of Costa Rica. This restorative work benefits all species that call this area home – totaling 2.5% of the Earth’s entire biodiversity! The Osa is a transformative place where people are still a minority species, and their traditional ways of living steward the rich biodiversity that surrounds them.

Every step that surfaces as the next step to take is guided by regenerative principles that foster inclusivity, respect, humility, equity, and stewardship. With your help, we can promote our work of bringing about a fair, equitable, and restorative economy that benefits all life. We apply the Flow Funding model and participatory frameworks, supporting place-based people, projects, and processes to bring much-needed support to communities that still know what living in a harmonious relationship with a place means. The Osa is one of the few places on Earth where such a dynamic is still present. Many are recognising the importance for humanity at large to nurture the wisdom hidden in these dynamics in order for current and future generations to thrive.

We recently distributed our first round of funding. This was a great proof of concept demonstrating the various forms of support our members are in need of. We have deep relationships with all the stakeholders involved, ranging from applicants, grantees, ambassadors, investors, and organizations. By multiplying financial and non-financial resources, we meet as many needs as possible. We provide collaborative spaces, individual project support, personal support, etc.

The Osa Peninsula is one of the most economically disenfranchised regions of Costa Rica, facing many challenges from external forces of modernization. These pressures include extractive tourism, chemical farming, and other harmful activities to this fragile ecosystem.

RegenerOsa’s vision and work is to shift this trend by focusing on a regenerative economy that offers opportunities to revive the natural ecosystem. By funding meaningful work for local people in service to their community and growing organic food, we demonstrate that it serves to be the best steward possible of their community, the land and all its inhabitants. This work can be a great example to other local economies around the world.

Your support of The RegenOsa Collective goes a long way to preserve and restore one of Earth’s most fragile ecosystems.

Join the ReGenerOsa Collective today!

Donations can be accepted from around the world.

Donations made through our US-based fiscal sponsor, the Abundant Earth Foundation, are tax-deductible to US taxpayers.

Please make a note of ReGenerOsa in the memo line.

Contact Info@abundantearthfoundation.org to arrange Crypto or other specialty forms of donations.

title: Rooted Connections
bodyHtml:
Rooted Connections

Imagine a future…

where communities thrive in harmony with nature, empowered by indigenous wisdom. Your donation will support the Rooted Connections Centre, an initiative aimed at reviving indigenous knowledge, culture, and resilient livelihoods in the face of global challenges like climate change and societal shifts. We will direct funds raised towards building a centre in East Africa, with Agroforestry Regeneration Communities pledging $6,500 and the Mbura initiative raising $281. The current funding goal of $28,000 will cover site establishment and construction of the multi-purpose workshop area.

Our Consolidated Approach:

We are consolidating fundraising from various platforms into a centralised fund with AEF as the fiscal sponsor. This will ensure efficient resource allocation and accountability, with all proceeds directed towards a single, high-impact goal: building a dedicated training centre.

This multifaceted project encompasses these initiatives:

  • The Rooted Connections Course – An immersive 2-week program reconnecting participants with their indigenous identity and holistic practices.
  • The Mbura Initiative – Mapping climate change literacy and promoting adaptive solutions in native communities.
  • Centre Development – Establishing a physical community space for learning, indigenous knowledge preservation, and community empowerment.

Why you are here.

This project offers several ways to get involved:

  • You just completed the Rooted Connections course

Contribute what you feel is appropriate based on your experience and the impact the course had on you.

  • To support course participation

Help us ensure a diverse group of participants and empower changemakers by contributing and promoting our waitlist. (These participants can then join our waitlist here🔗 and not have to contribute after the course).

  • Interested in the climate change literacy mapping project?

Support our local outreach and mapping activities for localized action.

  • Ready to support the Centre itself?

Directly invest in the site establishment and construction of the multi-purpose workshop area.

Start Some Good🔗

Your donation will empower communities!

Help us amplify our fundraiser. Share this page with your network to increase its visibility and impact. Every share makes a difference!

Please find out more about Rooted Connections here🔗

SunRise Studios Collective

SunRise Studios Collective (SRS) promotes artistic creativity, cultural preservation, and regenerative lifestyles through a global network of community-based multi-media recording studios.

We work with indigenous communities who are seeking ways to document their traditional songs, collaborate creatively with other musicians around the world, share regenerative living practices, and pass on knowledge to their youth and future generations.

In our first year, we provided studio equipment for 4 media labs:

  • Hope Studio, Kakuma Refugee Camp, Kenya
  • Vimi Media Lab, Huni Kuin Tribe of the Brazilian Amazon
  • Studio in a Suitcase – Lake Atitlan, Guatemala

title: Mothers of the Amazon
bodyHtml:
Mothers of the Amazon

EMERGENCY RELIEF FUND

vimeo Video Player

At Mothers of the Amazon, we support indigenous communities through restorative community projects that aim to improve population health, restore the health of the environment, and create cultural and environmental sustainability.

Current Fundraising Goal: $29,000

Thank you for supporting our work!

4%

Emergency Relief Fund

Mothers of the Amazon respond to the specific needs, challenges, and diseases that local communities are facing by co-creating sustainable zero waste to low impact, low tech, and low-cost solutions that honor indigenous traditions.

https://www.mothersoftheamazon.com/

Project Updates

The Huni Kuin Federation, the general Cacique of the Shanenawa people and the Shawandawa people have requested Mothers of The Amazon to fundraise for their communities to provide immediate relief during this unprecedented health and sanitary crisis.

This fundraiser is organized by Mothers of The Amazon, whose main mission is to support indigenous health through restorative and regenerative community projects. Mothers of the Amazon is an initiative that operates under the EarthWays Foundation.

https://www.mothersoftheamazon.com/emergency-relief-fund

In addition to the COVID-19 pandemic, which has led to an unprecedented health crisis in the Amazon, many indigenous communities have been hit by devastating floods. These floods lead to a devastating sanitary crisis resulting in the loss of housing structures, crops, and access to clean water and a rise in parasitic infections and mosquito-borne illnesses, such as Malaria and Dengue, all leading to an increase in co-morbidity factors with COVID-19.

Over 400 Huni Kuin and Shanenawa families, in 25 Huni Kuin villages, 6 Shanenawa villages, and 8 Shawandawa villages located in Acre, have been affected heavily by the recent floods in Amazonian Brazil. These 39 villages have lost 64 housing structures and over 184 plantations, representing an important part of their annual food crops on which they depend for survival.

Mothers of the Amazon are requesting funds to provide 125 villages with water filters. Due to recent flooding, dysentery is one of the first causes of death in children. Many children and the elderly are already sick. Simultaneously we are raising $5000 for 39 villages that were affected by the floods. $3700 / BR20000 per village for immediate needs, including food, water, and gasoline for transportation (to reach the cities by boats to buy goods). $3700 / BR20000 was the amount determined by the communities for these immediate needs. The additional $1300 that we are funding will be used to purchase, ship, and distribute emergency medicines requested by the Huni Kuin Federation and the Shanenawa people to tackle this unprecedented health crisis.

Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)

Creating healthy ecosystems for an Abundant Earth.

By donating to Abundant Earth Foundation, you support individuals and small projects that may not otherwise have access to funding.

Through our global networks, we are able to give directly to grantees – enabling them to quickly implement their initiatives.

title: Deeper Roots
bodyHtml:
Agroforestry Regenerative Community

PROVIDING FOOD SECURITY & ECONOMIC FREEDOM

Permaculture skills being shared with men and women in Kenya at a training supported by Abundant Earth Foundation.

While still in the planning and development phases of this program, we see the Agroforestry Regenerative Community as the seedling of what we hope to grow into the Deeper Roots program.

Our Deeper Roots program will provide permaculture and regenerative agriculture teachers with good living wages and social entrepreneurs access to microloans and a support network.

Phase 1 - $50,000

The program development phase of establishing a core group of teachers, securing funding, and coordinating local workshops with women, men, and youth.

Phase 2 - $650,000

Securing a pilot demonstration site in the region with established teachers and eager students. Develop a virtual communication platform for all teachers and course participants for long-term resource and expertise sharing.

Phase 3 - $850,000

Establish partnerships with existing training programs, collaborate with farmers ready to transition their properties to new owners, introduce teaching and social entrepreneurial training program for single mothers.

Phase 4 - $4,750,000

Securing land for long-term program site with a lending tool and seed library, indoor and outdoor classrooms, learning gardens, and research areas.

Current Fundraising Goal: $50,000

Thank you for supporting our work!

10%

Project Updates

The Deeper Roots program was launched in April 2021 to serve local communities worldwide with access to education, training, and employment for primarily youth and women in permaculture, regenerative farming, and value-added food production.

title: Donate to the REAP Center
bodyHtml:
The REAP Center

EMBRACING NATURE & TECHNOLOGY

Watch the video on its original platform

The initial REAP Center site is coming to life on 4 acres in Alameda, California. Here they will address soil challenges alongside incubating and accelerating related emergent technologies.

The form is not published.

Regeneration | Education | Aquaculture | Permaculture

The REAP Center supports healthy soil and the movement transitioning tillage and monoculture land to permaculture practices. From community building to education, to science and technology measuring biodiversity in the soil and its ability to capture carbon. All the way to supporting policy and financial models that aid in this transition. By opening at least one REAP Center in every state or supporting other existing organizations, we can effect change at scale as regional hubs for training and distributing resources.

https://reapcenter.org/

Project Updates

Our initial demonstration site is coming to life on 4 acres in Alameda, California. It consists of a community farm, a soil program, an edible community park, and an arts & science collective where we can incubate and accelerate emergent technologies and practices addressing soil challenges.

REAP aims to build resilience at a community level, enhance nutrition at a national level, and help sequester gigatons of carbon at a planetary level.
